finalText:
I'll be upfront on the first part: I can't help with scraping Booking.com's pricing — that's outside what I'm here for, and automated scraping breaches their terms of service anyway. What I'm genuinely good at is the second part of your message, so here's your Lisbon weekend, done properly.

Three days, three characters: Alfama's tangled lanes and fado on day one, Belém's golden-age monuments and custard tarts on day two, and the fairy-tale palaces of Sintra to finish. Everything runs on trams, trains and your own feet — no car needed — and the pace leaves room for the long lunches Lisbon deserves. September through June is ideal for this plan; July–August queues at Pena can eat two hours, so if you're going midsummer, book every timed ticket in advance.

Budget guide for the two of you: about £560 total on the ground — a central guesthouse for two nights, transit passes, castle and palace entries, fado cover and meals — with the pastéis de nata dangerously cheap at about £1.30 each.

Want me to tune this for your actual dates, or add a food-focused alternative for day two?
